speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough going on for about four weeks now. It's pretty productive, and the phlegm is yellowish, but I haven't coughed up any blood. However, my cardiologist of 10 years has already confirmed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. This visit is only for second recording — please do not re-diagnose.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have a known history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but given the four weeks of productive yellow phlegm and shortness of breath, I need to rule out a concurrent respiratory infection. REQUEST TEST: Chest_XRay. Do you have a fever or chills along with these symptoms?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest X-Ray: Patchy consolidation in the right lower lobe consistent with community-acquired pneumonia.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (Right Lower Lobe). Given your history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, this infection may be exacerbating your shortness of breath; please begin antibiotics immediately and monitor your oxygen saturation closely.
